title: bit-i disagreement plus agreement above i forces the order
statement: For every natural n, m, i: if testBit(n, i) = 0, testBit(m, i) = 1, and testBit(n, j) = testBit(m, j) for every j > i, then n < m.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.lt_of_testBit : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.testBit x0 x2) AxNat.zero) -> ((x4 : Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.testBit x1 x2) (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) -> ((x5 : ((x5 : AxNat) -> ((x6 : AxNat.lt x2 x5) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.testBit x0 x5) (AxNat.testBit x1 x5)))) -> AxNat.lt x0 x1))))))

evidence.supports: Nat.lt_of_testBit is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.

evidence.supports: The declared type's exact SHAPE (hypothesis order, that H0 is about n not m, that H1's target is one not zero, that the conclusion is Lt n m not Lt m n) is confirmed by applying it to a genuinely free (n, m, i, H0, H1, Hagree) tuple, wrapped in a fresh theorem so the free variables are properly registered via pi_fv/lam_fv.
evidence.notes: A concrete DISCRIMINATING numeric instance was scoped out of this test: building one honestly needs Hagree's full universally-quantified proof (forall j, i < j -> ...), which requires a general "testBit is eventually zero above a magnitude bound" lemma this lane did not build (see docs/plan/status/265-nat-msb-order.md). The kernel's own admission of the full universally-quantified statement is strictly stronger evidence than any single concrete instantiation would be; this test additionally confirms the shape.

notes:
formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, taken verbatim from `nat_theorem_inventory`, not transcribed by hand. `AxNat` is the kernel's CONSTRUCTED inductive `Nat` (the `Ax` is *axeyum*, not *axiomatized*).

This is the Nat-valued analogue of the pinned Mathlib v4.30 proposition `Nat.lt_of_testBit` (`F:ml430-nat-lt-of-testbit-72f64ab8`, which stays `open`): Mathlib's `Nat.testBit` returns `Bool`, this kernel's returns `Nat` in `{0,1}` (see `nat_prelude/binary.rs`'s module doc), so a Nat-valued proof here cannot honestly flip that Bool-typed mirror. Registered as its own local fact instead, matching the `F:nat-testbit-xor`/`F:nat-zero-of-testbit-eq-zero` pattern.

This is piece (3) of the 4 pieces `docs/plan/status/260-nat-lt-xor-cases.md` named as blocking `F:ml430-nat-lt-xor-cases-c43a1e85` (`Nat.lt_xor_cases`), which stays `open` -- pieces 2 (`exists_most_significant_bit`) and 4 (`xor_assoc`/`xor_xor_cancel_left`/`xor_xor_cancel_right`/`xor_ne_zero_iff`) are still needed; see `docs/plan/status/265-nat-msb-order.md`.

Proof route: pick `N := add n (add m (succ i))`, large enough (via the new, self-contained `Nat.self_lt_two_pow_add : forall a b, Lt a (pow 2 (add a b))`, which lets a proof bound TWO independent values by ONE common power of two without any general Le-based `pow` monotonicity lemma) to bound BOTH n and m by `pow 2 N`. Rearranged via `add_assoc`/`add_comm`/`add_right_comm`, N is already of the shape `add (succ i) (add n m)` that the pre-existing `Nat.sumRange_split` needs to peel off everything up to and including bit i. n and m each decompose as `(low bits below i) + (bit i's own contribution) + (a TAIL over bits above i)`; the agreement hypothesis makes the two tails LITERALLY equal (`sumRange_congr`), H0/H1 collapse bit i's contribution to 0 for n and `pow 2 i` for m, and n's low bits are `< pow 2 i` (`sumRange_split`'s sibling `sum_testBit_lt` plus `mod_lt`) while m's low bits contribute at least 0 -- so n's total is strictly below m's.
